newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIA'S GAZPROM SAYS IN TURKMEN GAS VENTURE.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA'S GAZPROM SAYS IN TURKMEN GAS VENTURE.

text.p: Russia's Gazprom natural gas monopoly reasserted control over Turkmen gas supplies on Thursday, saying it would work exclusively with Turkmenistan to supply the Central Asian state's gas to former Soviet republics.

Gazprom board chairman Rem Vyakhirev told a news conference the new company would replace the recently disbanded Turkmenrosgaz joint venture, which grouped Gazprom, state concern Turkmenneftegaz and Itera of the United States.
"The presidents (of Turkmenistan and Russia) have agreed that a new company will be created with Gazprom and Turkmenistan," Vyakhirev said.
Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov met Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Vyakhirev in Moscow to discuss Turkmenistan's energy situation, which has been in crisis for most of this year.

Niyazov disbanded Turkmenrosgaz in March, halting its exports of natural gas and sending the Central Asian state's economy, which is heavily dependent upon gas export revenues, into severe contraction.
Turkmenrosgaz was set up in 1996 to transport Turkmen gas to consumers in the former Soviet republics via Russian pipelines, which are controlled by Gazprom.
In the old venture, Gazprom had allowed Turkmenistan to export some gas to Europe via Russian pipelines.

Vyakhirev did not say how the new venture would operate or what stake Gazprom would hold, but his announcement seemed to reassert Russia's and Gazprom's control over gas supplies from the former Soviet republics.
"There is an agreement between the presidents to work on the CIS markets," Vyakhirev said. He did not say whether Gazprom would give Turkmenistan access to Russian pipelines to Europe.

Russia has the world's largest proven gas reserves, or about 35 percent of the total, and Turkmenistan the world's ninth-largest, or about two percent. Its unproven reserves could be many times larger.
